attested.notes: Halving pass against the over-humanising rule. Removed nine manufactured devices, all invented specificity or filler: rebuilding nine months of bank statements, shareholders funding a house purchase, the loan account found in month seven, the van sold to a brother-in-law last spring, 'we have seen that happen more than once', 'somebody writing it down', 'the question behind the question', 'the single most effective thing', and a duplicate of the Companies-House-panic observation that already appears in its proper section. Replaced with material derived from facts already on the page rather than from claimed experience: that debt size barely affects appointment speed while missing records and disagreeing shareholders do; that most MVL money reaches shareholders long before the 338-day median has run; that a long case is not the same as a demanding one; that the options before a petition is issued are wider than after. Deliberate devices remaining are the sourced Insolvency Service judgement, the seven-day adverts warning, one practitioner observation about directors checking Companies House at eighteen months, and the undisclosed-loan-account insight. Scene count deliberately low: the two remaining are genuine, and the old three-per-thousand quota has been removed from the pack as the cause of the invention.
